html:
Candombe is a drumming and dance tradition of the Afro-Uruguayan people of Montevideo. Groups of drummers parade through the streets of the old neighbourhoods of Sur and Palermo. UNESCO listed it as intangible heritage in 2009.

It grew from the gatherings of enslaved and free Africans in Montevideo in the 1700s and 1800s, when the city was a major port of the slave trade for the region. Three kinds of barrel-shaped drums, played with hand and stick, lock together in rhythm.

Each February, during Carnival, the Llamadas parade brings thousands of drummers and dancers into the streets. Candombe influenced tango and the popular music of Uruguay, and is a sign of an African heritage the country long overlooked.
